summary: Full-extraction pass on 19 stored documents (Grenada CBI/IMA statistics sheets, Grenada IMF reports and S.R.O. 15/2024, Saint Lucia CIU annual reports, regulations and IMF RCF report, the Dominica copy of IMF WP/15/93, and an Antigua CIU statement). observations.location: p. 1, row 'CBI Estimated Revenues*', Apr-23 column
observations.notes: Gross amounts calculated from applications approved by Cabinet in the period ('Is based on applications approved by Cabinet irrespective of the calendar year in which the application was received'), not cash received. category=ntf: NTF donations; budgetary_fees / project_government_contribution: government fees/contributions on the approved-project route; approved_projects / project_due_to_developers: investment due to developers of approved projects; other_fees / related_fees: other fees. This sheet prints no currency (amounts bare or with '$'); recorded as EC$ like the other rows from it, because the same Ministry template states 'Figures are quoted in Eastern Caribbean Dollars' (Oct-Dec 2022 sheet) and the amounts match EC$ conversions of the US$ prices (e.g. NTF US$200,000 x 2.7 = EC$540,000 per approval). First published version of the April-June 2023 sheet; the Ministry later replaced it (grd-mof-cbistats-2023q2-v2), so treat figures that differ there as superseded.

The total is the sum of the transfer to the Treasury for budgetary support (90% of NTF, recorded as cbi_transfers_to_government), debt reduction, NTF operating expenses and the contingency fund allocation (10% of NTF). This sheet prints no currency (amounts bare or with '$'); recorded as EC$ like the other rows from it, because the same Ministry template states 'Figures are quoted in Eastern Caribbean Dollars' (Oct-Dec 2022 sheet) and the amounts match EC$ conversions of the US$ prices (e.g. NTF US$200,000 x 2.7 = EC$540,000 per approval). First published version of the April-June 2023 sheet; the Ministry later replaced it (grd-mof-cbistats-2023q2-v2), so treat figures that differ there as superseded.

observations.location: p. 1, row 'CBI Estimated Revenues*', Apr-23 column
observations.notes: Gross amounts calculated from applications approved by Cabinet in the period ('Is based on applications approved by Cabinet irrespective of the calendar year in which the application was received'), not cash received. category=ntf: NTF donations; budgetary_fees / project_government_contribution: government fees/contributions on the approved-project route; approved_projects / project_due_to_developers: investment due to developers of approved projects; other_fees / related_fees: other fees. This sheet prints no currency (amounts bare or with '$'); recorded as EC$ like the other rows from it, because the same Ministry template states 'Figures are quoted in Eastern Caribbean Dollars' (Oct-Dec 2022 sheet) and the amounts match EC$ conversions of the US$ prices (e.g. NTF US$200,000 x 2.7 = EC$540,000 per approval). Updated version of the April-June 2023 sheet, replacing grd-mof-cbistats-2023q2-v1.

This sheet prints no currency (amounts bare or with '$'); recorded as EC$ like the other rows from it, because the same Ministry template states 'Figures are quoted in Eastern Caribbean Dollars' (Oct-Dec 2022 sheet) and the amounts match EC$ conversions of the US$ prices (e.g. NTF US$200,000 x 2.7 = EC$540,000 per approval).

events.title: NTF to pass first EC$2 million a month to the budget for arrears
events.description: Under the IMF-supported programme the National Transformation Fund will transfer through the budget to the CBI Fund the first EC$2 million of its monthly inflows, to settle supplier arrears by end-2015.
events.location: PDF p. 42, Annex II para 3; PDF p. 60, MEFP para 10
events.quote: NTF will transfer through the budget to the CBI Fund the first EC$2 million of its monthly inflows for the settlement of arrears.

events.title: Fiscal rules cap CBI receipts counted toward primary balance at 1.5% of GDP from 2018
events.description: The fiscal responsibility legislation (approved by Parliament in June 2015) reserves part of CBI receipts for budget financing and contingencies: 40 percent of monthly NTF inflows are saved, and the CBI receipts used to meet primary balance targets are capped at 1.5 percent of GDP from 2018 onward.
events.location: PDF p. 62, Annex on the fiscal responsibility framework, para 5
events.quote: the total sum of CBI program receipts to be used for meeting the primary balance targets are capped at 1.5 percent of GDP from 2018 onward.

events.title: Cap of 500 approved applications removed
events.description: The 2017 amendment regulations removed the limit of 500 applications the Board could grant, dropped the requirement for an affidavit declaring financial resources of at least US$3 million, added a US$50,000 non-refundable administration fee for the bond option and lowered the NEF amounts.
events.quote: Removing the limit of the number of applications which could be granted by the Board previously set at a maximum of 500

events.title: CIU to keep 20% of each NEF contribution for marketing
events.description: Amendment regulations (SI No. 1 of 2017, deemed in force 1 January 2017) let the Board retain twenty per cent of each monetary contribution to the National Economic Fund for marketing and promotion of the programme.
events.quote: The Board shall retain twenty per cent of each monetary contribution to the Saint Lucia National Economic Fund for the marketing and promotion

events.title: All CBI fees paid to the budget to be saved under the ECF programme
events.description: Under the IMF-supported programme all CBI fees paid to the budget are saved for direct and contingent financing, with supplier arrears repaid first; the IMF says this means 25 to 100 percent of CBI inflows available to the public sector (budget fees and NTF) are saved, depending on the mix of applicants between the NTF and investment options.
events.quote: This ensures that between 25 and 100 percent of the CBI inflows available to the public sector

new_indicators.name: CBI money due to the government (calculated)
new_indicators.definition: Amount of CBI money that a programme's statistics calculate as due to the government from applications approved in a period (budget fees and the government's share of fund contributions, e.g. savings and grants for capital spending), before it is collected or transferred. As defined by the source; use breakdown category= for its parts.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-grd-lca-dma-atg for Grenada's Ministry of Finance CBI statistics ('Amounts Due to Government', 2022; 'Earmarked for general government financing', 2019, a running total). Not cash: compare cbi_transfers_to_government.

ledger.contains: CIU news statement of 4 July 2017 answering a newspaper story on discrepancies in the 2015 six-monthly reports. A table for five 'countries of origin' (Iran, Iraq, Egypt, Lebanon, Turkey/Istanbul) with applications received (inception 2013 to December 2015) and passports issued, plus text giving approvals and persons granted citizenship for some of them. All extracted (breakdown country=, since 'country of origin' is not defined). The rest is narrative (who benefits from the programme) without numbers.

IMF Working Paper WP/15/93 (May 2015) on managing inflows from economic citizenship programmes. Same PDF (same SHA-256) as sources intl-imf-wp-15-93 and kna-imf-wp-15-93. Dominica content: Table 1 (inception 1993, minimum USD 100,000; already recorded), Table 3 (contribution to government US$100,000, or US$50,000 plus real estate US$200,000; added as terms), Box 1 (ECP fees to the budget under 1% of GDP in 2008 and 3.4% in 2013; both now recorded) and a Dominica chart without printed values. Everything else is about other programmes (St. Kitts and Nevis SIDF tables, Malta, Portugal, US EB-5, Pacific trust funds) or general policy.
ledger.to_do: Non-Dominica content is not extracted under this source id, to avoid a third copy of the same rows: Table 1 minimum investments for the other 19 programmes, Table 3 columns for Antigua, Grenada, St. Kitts, Cyprus and Malta, Box 5 SIDF expenditure/surplus lines, SIDF direct spending table and consolidated SIDF/government account, Box 2 KNA fiscal balance statistics, Malta (1,800 cap, 50-100 approvals a year, EUR 650,000 contribution), Portugal (EUR 1.11 billion since Oct 2012; 75-80% of Golden Visas to Chinese) and US EB-5 (81% Chinese in 2013). Extract these once under intl-imf-wp-15-93 or kna-imf-wp-15-93. Figures 1, 2a and the Box 1 charts have no printed values.

ledger.contains: IMF 2022 Article IV staff report for Grenada. CBI appears only in text: CBI revenues 'stable at 4 percent of GDP' (already recorded), NTF used for grants and a contingency fund, CBI used mainly for real estate and planned hotels, EU Parliament criticism. The fiscal tables include CBI inside non-tax revenue and grants without a separate CBI line, and the balance of payments has no CBI line, so there is nothing more to extract.

IMF first ECF review for Grenada (Dec 2014). Annex II on the new CBI programme: visa-free access table (event exists), fee schedule as of August 2014 (NTF and private-investment rows already recorded; the two 'tranche' rows added as terms), the rule that all budget fees are saved (25-100% of public-sector inflows; added as event), the NTF's monthly EC$2 million transfer for arrears (added as event), and a staff estimate that budget receipts could be 0.2-0.6% of GDP a year (added as a projection range). Fiscal tables have no separate CBI line.

IMF second ECF review for Grenada (Jul 2015). CBI numbers: receipts of EC$5.4 million (around 0.2% of GDP) Sept 2014-Mar 2015 (EC$ figure existed; percent added), budget counting on CBI inflows of 4¼% of GDP in 2015 (existed), MEFP: 2015 budget assumes NTF inflows of 4% of GDP plus EC$24 million (1% of GDP) for arrears (added), Table 3 transfer from the NTF for arrears 24.0 in 2015 (added), and rules: 40% of NTF inflows saved (event exists from another source), CBI receipts counted toward primary balance capped at 1.5% of GDP from 2018 (event added), creditors' share of CBI revenue above US$15 million a year (event exists), quarterly publication of CBI statistics (event exists).

One-page Ministry of Finance 'Citizenship by Investment Statistics' sheet for October-December 2019 (months and quarter): applications received, approved and rejected by Cabinet and new citizens, each split NTF/investment; amounts due calculated from approvals (NTF, budgetary fees, approved projects) for the month and year to date; NTF eligible revenues and fees; amounts earmarked for general government financing (year to date); CBI payments to the Treasury (NTF section 10, CBI section 11, dividends); Treasury CBI account balance; Treasury spending from CBI (monthly and cumulative). All extracted. The 'Arrear repayment/other financing' line has a single '-' and the eligible-revenues block prints only the fees sub-line (the total equals NTF due plus fees). No currency printed; recorded as EC$ like the existing row.

One-page Ministry of Finance 'Citizenship by Investment Statistics' sheet for October-December 2022 (EC$): applications received, approved, rejected and new citizens by NTF/investment; amounts due by NTF, budgetary fees, other fees and approved projects, monthly and year to date (the running total leaves out other fees); NTF eligible revenues; amounts due to government (budget fees, 40% NTF savings, grants for capital spending); Treasury spending from CBI, monthly and cumulative. All extracted; the 'Debt reduction/contingency financing' line is blank.

One-page Ministry of Finance 'Citizenship by Investment Statistics' sheet for January-March 2023: applications received, approved, rejected and new citizens by NTF/approved project; CBI estimated revenues (NTF, government contribution, related fees, due to developers) monthly and year to date; NTF eligible revenues; NTF usage (transfer to Treasury 90%, debt reduction, operating expenses, contingency 10%) and an 'Approved Projects' line outside the total. All extracted; quarter totals differ from the months by 1 in a few rows (rounding).

One-page Ministry of Finance 'Citizenship by Investment Statistics' sheet for April-June 2023, first published version: same template as Q1 2023. All extracted as provisional. In this version the printed year-to-date total leaves out related fees (April 315,900,000 vs parts 338,096,453), and May new citizens (75) and applications received differ from the updated version.

One-page Ministry of Finance 'Citizenship by Investment Statistics' sheet for April-June 2023, updated version replacing the first one: same template as Q1 2023. All extracted; parts add up to totals (quarter totals differ by 1 in two rows, rounding).

One-page Ministry of Finance 'Citizenship by Investment Statistics' sheet for July-September 2023: same template as Q1 2023. All extracted; parts add up (1-dollar rounding differences in two quarter totals and two running totals).

One-page Ministry of Finance 'Citizenship by Investment Statistics' sheet for October-December 2023: same template as Q1 2023 (related fees negative in October and November). All extracted; parts add up.

One-page Investment Migration Agency fiscal performance sheet (Ministry of Finance) for October-December 2024, months and quarter: IMA revenues by NTF contribution, NTF application and processing fees, approved-project government contribution, application and processing fees and related fees; IMA outflows (commission, refunds, fees); net revenue; notes with NTF eligible revenue for the bond calculation agent, NTF transfers (budgetary support 90%, contingency fund 10%) and contingency fund opening, transfer and closing balances. All extracted; parts add up to totals (one-cent rounding in a few quarter totals). The title says '(EC$M)' but figures are in EC dollars.

One-page Investment Migration Agency fiscal performance sheet (Ministry of Finance) for October-December 2025, months and quarter: IMA revenues by NTF contribution, NTF application and processing fees, approved-project government contribution, application and processing fees and related fees; IMA outflows (commission, refunds, fees); net revenue; notes with NTF eligible revenue for the bond calculation agent, NTF transfers (budgetary support 90%, contingency fund 10%) and contingency fund opening, transfer and closing balances. All extracted; parts add up to totals (one-cent rounding in a few quarter totals).

Grenada S.R.O. 15 of 2024 (in force 1 July 2024): replacement Schedule I with NTF amounts (US$235,000 for main applicant and up to 3 dependants; US$25,000/50,000/75,000 per extra dependant by type), approved-project minimum US$350,000 and shared unit US$270,000 per share (total US$540,000), government contributions for approved projects and significant investments (US$50,000 plus 25,000/50,000/75,000 per dependant), and developer fees (application US$10,000, due diligence US$7,500 each for developer and directors, project administration US$20,000 a year, start-date extension US$10,000). All recorded as program terms; repeals S.R.O. 12 of 2024.

Saint Lucia S.I. No. 1 of 2017 (deemed in force 1 Jan 2017): CIU Board retains 20% of each NEF contribution (event added); oath of allegiance before listed officials; US$50,000 non-refundable administration fee for the bond option; NEF minimums US$100,000 alone, US$165,000 with spouse, US$190,000 with spouse and up to two dependants, US$25,000 per extra dependant (all added as terms); revokes S.I. 105 of 2016 and reg. 7(3) and (9) of the 2015 regulations (no numbers).

Saint Lucia CIU annual report 2015/16 (first six-month period Oct 2015-Mar 2016): set-up of the Unit, staff, policies; approved real estate projects (2 approved by Cabinet, 2 more pending, with gross development costs); two citizenship applications received (table by country of birth, both NEF donations); agents and marketing agreements; revenue table by fee type (actual and budget, EC$); grant income, programme costs, due diligence fees, operating expenses, deficit; no investment inflows and no transfers to government.
